To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
agricultural interests are still important in the EC policy-making process but their influence is more indirect than in the past.
the agricultural interests in the EC policy-making process are still very important, but that their role is changing and will change even more.

the agricultural interests in the various member states are increasingly integrated into the overall EC ‘crisis’ management, which means that the segmentation in relation the CAP is weakened, but that the segmentation in the national policy-making process is strengthened, because national governments are the central players in EC policy-making and because the national agricultural organizations have a growing interest to emphasize joint activities and mutual agreements on fundamental agricultural issues on the EC level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the national interest organizations on the EC policy-making process and their ability to influence EC decisions.

the question of the role and influence of agricultural interests in the EC policy-making process, in particular the role of national agricultural interests and the role of the national interest organizations in relation to the EC interest organization COPA.
the following question: What are the conditions and the impact of agricultural interests on the EC policy-making process, especially in the present economic crisis?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
national agricultural organizations will have to concentrate on the national level and on bread-and-butter agreements with national governments in the future.

the national interest organizations have a greater impact on EC agricultural policy-making than is generally assumed, because they are able to influence the strategies of their respective national governments.

the role of agricultural interest organizations in Community policy-making will be determined by the extent to which national governments succeed in their attempt to maintain the national interest organizations as a ‘safety valve’ for the promotion of national interests in the policy-making process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the national agricultural organizations are in a process of change, and that the future of these organizations will be decided by their ability to adjust to the new situation.
the role of agricultural interests in the EC policy-making process is changing in a direction that will make the role of COPAs less important in EC policy-making.
the national governments and national agricultural organizations will be more important for the EC policy-making process than before.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the national interest organizations are still the key players, and that the national level remains the key level for the agricultural interests.
agricultural interests are not as important as the literature suggests, but that the importance of agricultural interests depends on the context in which policy-making is taking place.

the agricultural interest organizations in the various member states, as a consequence of their national interest organization-government relationships, have been more inclined to pursue national interests in the EC policy-making process than to pursue common interests.
